audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Gnar levels 3, 4-5, first item and 2 items, but the whys underneath say the opposite: whys[1] and whys[2] both describe Fiora winning levels 2 and 3 outright, whys[3] calls 4-5 a Rage-bar coin flip, and whys[5] says the first-item window 'still beats mini-Gnar'. The packet levelChart reads Fiora / Fiora / Fiora / Skill / Fiora / Skill / Gnar.
audit.why: Mini Gnar has no stun at all — Hyper (W) is a passive damage buff in that form and Hop (E) is a 22s escape at rank 1. Fiora's Q is 13s falling to 6s and refunds on a Vital, so she out-chains him at 2 and 3. The lane only turns once he can hold a full Rage bar through a trade and once Boomerang range plus items let him kite from outside her 400-unit Lunge.
audit.corrected: Level 2 -> Fiora, Level 3 -> Fiora, Levels 4-5 -> Skill, First item -> Skill; Level 1, Level 6 and 2+ items already correct. Flipped as one atomic group in both layers.

audit.why: The four spikes are right and well-ordered: 2-3 mini punish, 6 Grand Challenge, the Mega timer, and 2 items. Only the phase whys needed the actual numbers attached.
audit.corrected: Added the 90s rank-1 GNAR! cooldown to the first-item phase and the 22s Hop cooldown to Level 3.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2] is titled 'Stand near walls for Mega-E'. The wall-stun does not come from E — Mega Gnar's E (Crunch) is a slam that deals area damage on landing. The terrain stun is GNAR! (R), which throws enemies and stuns any that hit a wall.
audit.why: Kit text: E 'Mega Gnar is too large to bounce and instead lands with earth-shattering force, dealing damage in an area around him'; R 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage'. The content layer already gets this right in spikes[2] and late — only the full layer's don't is wrong.
audit.corrected: Retitled to GNAR! and stated the real interaction plus its 90s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.why: The Riposte interaction is stated correctly and is the decisive one: Wallop is an immobilise, so parrying it upgrades Fiora's W stab to a stun — but Riposte blocks only the first immobilise, so Wallop into GNAR! chains past it. Both content spikes[2] and wants.you[1] already say this.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', sequencingCues 0. Every window was phrased as 'when GNAR! is down' with no duration.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and is reduced when he catches it; Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s; Wallop is 7s; GNAR! is 90/60/30s. Those are the real windows.
audit.corrected: Put Boomerang's 16s, Hop's 22s and GNAR!'s 90s into the phase whys so each 'wait for X' is timed.

edits.before: W is your matchup answer; hold it for HIS key spell only. Only take the trade when Gnar's GNAR! is down.
edits.after: Trade after his Boomerang Throw leaves — it is a 16s cooldown at rank 1 unless he catches it on the return.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gnar must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online and mini-Gnar has no stun — his Hop is 22s at rank 1, so punish him the moment he spends it.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around GNAR!'s cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: A Rage-bar coin flip: run the pattern on an empty bar, and never start a fight the bar can fill before your Q comes back.

edits.before: Ravenous Hydra is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on GNAR!'s cooldown.
edits.after: Ravenous Hydra lands — force fights in mini form, while GNAR! sits on a 90s rank-1 cooldown.

edits.before: Gnar wastes GNAR! (Mega Stun) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: It damages on the way out and again returning — sidestep both halves.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Boomerang out-ranges your 400-unit Lunge — close the gap or leave.

edits.before: Burning Riposte on poke — your W exists to delete his ONE key spell; waste it and the duel maths flips against you.
edits.after: GNAR! throws you into terrain for a stun and bonus damage — fight in open ground, off his 90-second ultimate.

notes: The content layer here is already at the approved bar (spikes, early/mid/late and wants all match the kit text, including the Riposte-parries-Wallop-into-stun detail). The full layer was generic boilerplate with 'GNAR!' pasted into every slot, and its level chart contradicted the content whys and the packet. Mega Gnar's E is Crunch (area damage on landing), not a wall stun — the wall stun is GNAR! (R); the full layer's don't had that wrong and is corrected.
